method: Instruction listings decoded directly from the PE bytes of the identified executable through its section table, with the executable size and SHA-256 verified first. A script decoded each constructor linearly, took the pushed arguments of every call to the two record registrars 0x00443CF0 and 0x00443D50, tracked register operands through mov, xor, or and lea, and read each name and default literal from the string constructor 0x00447260 call that builds it. The string literals were read from the PE bytes. Callers were enumerated from a linear decode of the .text section, so virtual and indirect references are not covered. Addresses are absolute virtual addresses. No decompiled body is a tracked evidence dependency.
scope: The configuration stores that hold the values _getUserConfig, _setUserConfig, _saveUserConfig and _resetUserConfig address: the shared record model, the constructors that register every group, key, name, value type, range and default of the GameConfig, UserConfig and SystemConfig stores, the per-character file that overrides the GameConfig and UserConfig defaults, its text format and its override order. Client-side contracts do not establish what a retail character file contained or what a server sends.
evidenceTier: MIXED, see tierVocabulary and the tier of each fact

stores.name: GameConfig
stores.fact: The constructor at 0x004C4750 passes group count 7 through the ResourceConfig constructor 0x004B66F0 to 0x00444150, which stores it at +0x04 and allocates 7 * 32 records of 0xBC bytes at +0x08. The only caller 0x004DC12B constructs it at context +0x17430, the object 0x004D73C0 returns and the store every _getUserConfig call addresses. Its 145 registrar calls cover 139 distinct group and key pairs. The other 6 are the alternate defaults of group 4 keys 0 to 5.

stores.name: UserConfig
stores.fact: The constructor at 0x004BB3D0 passes group count 6 to 0x004B66F0 and registers its records through 0x004B6C60. Its context store at +0x174C8 is distinct from the GameConfig store. The natives of the desktop contracts do not address it.

stores.name: SystemConfig
stores.fact: The constructor at 0x004B8640 passes group count 10 straight to 0x00444150 and does not use the ResourceConfig constructor. Its only caller 0x0040179D passes this + 0x3A0, which agrees with the SystemConfig placement in manifests/structs.json. It registers 139 distinct group and key pairs.

recordModel.shared: The three stores share the Sqex::Misc::Config record model of constructor 0x00444150 (vftable 0x00F67290).

storeFields.0x0C: Dirty byte. Both registrars and the set accessors write 1. The path writer 0x00443ED0 clears it.

recordFields.0x00: Type tag. 0 is unregistered (set by the record constructor 0x00443C30), 1 is int and 2 is string.
recordFields.0x58: Range word one, the registrar argument 3. Type 1 only.
recordFields.0x5C: Range word two, the registrar argument 4. Type 1 only.
recordFields.0x60: Int value. Registered equal to the default.
recordFields.0x68: String value, a 0x54-byte inline Utf8String. For type 2 it is registered equal to the default string.

registrars.effect: Sets type 1, the name, +0x58 = min, +0x5C = max and +0x60 = +0x64 = default.
Sets type 2, the name and +0x68 = default.

accessors.role: Reads the int at +0x60 and returns its third argument when the computed record address (array pointer at +0x08 plus the record offset) is zero.
Copies +0x64 to +0x60 for a type 1 record.
Writes +0x60 and sets the dirty byte. No range test.
Writes +0x68 and sets the dirty byte.
Range test: true when the record is type 1 and +0x58 <= value <= +0x5C by signed compare.

rangeSemantics.claim: The two range words are an inclusive signed minimum and maximum. The setter 0x00443DD0, the Lua setter callback target 0x0075C980 and the file parser 0x004448E0 never test them. Besides the two text writers 0x00443ED0 and 0x00444730, the only code that reads both words is the range test 0x00444110, and neither a rel32 call nor an absolute reference to it exists in the image.

luaTargets.target: 0x0075C980 for an int value or 0x0075CA70 for a string value

recordModel.luaStore: All five targets resolve their store through 0x004D73C0, so Lua reaches only the GameConfig store.
recordModel.luaSetter: The int target 0x0075C980 calls 0x00443DD0 and then the change notifier 0x004B6780, which calls the listener held at +0x20 of the store. The reset target 0x0075C9C0 calls 0x00443DA0 for type 1 and 0x00443E00 with the empty string at 0x00FD866A for type 2, and jumps past the notifier for a type 0 record.

gameConfig.addressing: _getUserConfig(group, key) reaches native group = group - 1 and native key = key - 1. The Lua-facing ids in this manifest are the native ids plus one.
gameConfig.unregisteredKeys: A native key with no registrar call stays type 0 and _getUserConfig returns nil. Every group registers keys 0 to keyCount - 1, so group 0 leaves keys 19 to 31, group 2 key 31, group 3 keys 7 to 31, group 4 keys 9 to 31, group 5 keys 24 to 31 and group 6 keys 17 to 31 unregistered. Group 1 registers all 32 keys. The lookup 0x00443EA0 does not test the group against the group count, so group 7 and above address memory past the record array.

lowSpecSwitch.claim: Group 4 keys 0 to 5 are registered by one of two sequences. The constructor calls 0x00443E40 with (9, 12, 0) on the object it received as its fourth argument. A zero result falls through to the first sequence and a non-zero result jumps to 0x004C658F, the second sequence. The only store that registers group 9 key 12 is SystemConfig, where the name is low_spec_mode with default 0, so the object is taken to be SystemConfig. Keys 6 to 8 are registered by both paths with the same values.

groups.contents: chat window, macro, lock and targeting options
camera, name plate, key config, search sort and log font options
chat log filters, titles and enable flags
name plate visibility, map alpha and camera lock limit

userConfig.keyMapping: For slot 1 to 8 the four keys 4 * (slot - 1) + 0, 1, 2, 3 carry the parts x, y, w, h.
userConfig.fact: The routine loops group 0 to 5 and slot 1 to 8 and registers each of the 192 records through 0x00443CF0 with range -10000 to 10000 and default -1. The constructor 0x004BB3D0 calls it once.

systemConfig.note: The defaults are the values the constructor registers. They are not the values of a retail installation, which an installation file may override. The loading path of this store was not traced. Min, max and default are 32-bit words printed as signed values, so debuginfo_mode (group 0 key 2) has max 0xFFFFFFFF printed as -1 and view_clear_color (group 5 key 1) has default 0xAAAAAAAA printed as -1431655766 above its max 0x00FFFFFF. SystemConfig is not reached by any Lua native, so its rows carry native ids only. registeredKeyCount counts the keys a group registers, which are not contiguous for group 8 (keys 0, 1 and 8) and group 9 (keys 0 to 7 and 9 to 12).

gameAndUserFiles.claim: GameConfig and UserConfig are loaded from one file per character, named game and ui. The switch routine 0x004D9980 takes a character id. For a real id it calls 0x004B71F0 on the GameConfig store with the id, the name literal game (0x00F90DBC) and flag 0, and 0x004B67E0 on the UserConfig store with the name literal ui (0x00F90DC4). 0x004B71F0 also stores the id at +0x28 and the name at +0x30, which the save path reads. Both call slot 0x0C of the object held at +0x18 of the store, passing the id, the name, the store's own callback object (+0x10) and the flag, and skip the call when a file handle is already held at +0x1C.
gameAndUserFiles.pathLayout: root string + the sprintf of '\user\%08X\' (literal 0x00F672E8) with the character id + the file name. No extension is appended by the builder. The root is one of two process strings, 0x0132CC48 for flag 0 and 0x0132CCA0 for a non-zero flag, and both are filled at run time.

resourceModule.claim: The object at +0x18 of the store is taken to be a Component::Resource::ResourceModule, whose vftable 0x01108C3C holds 0x00C99480 at offset 0x0C and 0x00C98E40 at offset 0x14. Both take the 7 arguments the callers push, both call the path builder 0x0044AC40 and no other vftable in the image holds them.

sentinel.claim: 0xC0000000 means no character. Ten of the eleven call sites of 0x004D9980 push the constant. The other, 0x004DCC41, pushes a handler argument at ebp + 8 whose origin was not traced. The routine does nothing when the id equals the stored current id at context +0x1783C.

onLoaded.claim: When the file read completes the callback obtains the buffer pointer through virtual slot 8 and the byte count through virtual slot 10 of the file object, calls the parser 0x004448E0 on the store and sets the loaded byte at +0x15.

textFormat.intLine: name,<TAB>min,<TAB>max,<TAB>value then a newline, written by sprintf format 0x00F6726C and 0x00F67240 as %s,\t%d,\t%d,\t%d\n.
textFormat.stringLine: name,<TAB>value then a newline, written by format 0x00F6727C and 0x00F67250 as %s,\t%s\n. The writer replaces comma with 0x02, line feed with 0x03 and carriage return with 0x04 in the value and the parser reverses it.
parseRules: The text is split into lines and every line into fields at the separator set. A line whose first byte is # is skipped.
The record is found by exact name through 0x00444090, a linear scan over groupCount * 32 records. A line whose name matches no registered record is ignored.
A line with one field sets the string at +0x68 to the empty string.
A line with two fields sets the string at +0x68 to the second field after the 0x02, 0x03 and 0x04 replacement.
A line with four fields sets the int at +0x60 to the decimal parse (0x004555A0, base 10) of the fourth field. The min and max fields are not read.
Any other field count is ignored. The line type is not compared with the record type.
Lines are applied from the last line to the first, so the first line of a name is the one that remains.
textFormat.writer: The serializer 0x00444730 walks groupCount * 32 records in order, emits one line per type 1 or type 2 record and skips type 0. 0x004C71A0 writes it to the file created through slot 0x14 of the resource module and 0x004C72F0 is the wrapper that _saveUserConfig reaches.

pathWriter.claim: A second writer opens a path with mode wt, writes the two header lines at 0x00F67208 and 0x00F67228 (Shift-JIS comments that begin with # and name the columns), then the same line formats, and clears the dirty byte. It writes only when the dirty byte is set and has no rel32 caller or absolute reference.

overrideOrder: The constructor registers every record with value equal to default.

The constructor ends by serializing the registered values into a default text snapshot held at +0x84 (vector begin +0x88, end +0x8C) through 0x00444730. 0x004B7250 parses that snapshot back to restore the registered values.
Switching to a real character id opens that character's game file and, when it completes, overlays the values it names.

Switching to the sentinel writes the UserConfig store to the previous character's ui file, re-registers its records through 0x004B6C60, writes the GameConfig store to the game file through 0x004C72F0, parses the default snapshot, zeroes the result of 0x004D9910 held at context +0x17838 and runs 0x004D6A50, which sets group 3 keys 0, 1, 2, 5 and 4 to 100. The common tail then moves the current id at context +0x1783C to +0x17840 and stores the sentinel at +0x1783C.
persistence.changeNotification: The int and string set targets call 0x004B6780 with (0, group, key) after the write. The reset target 0x0075C9C0 calls it after a type 1 or type 2 reset and skips it for a type 0 record. 0x004B6780 forwards to the listener at +0x20 of the store when one is set.

boundaries: The values are the constructor defaults and the client's file handling. They do not establish what a retail character file held.

The run-time contents of the two root strings at 0x0132CC48 and 0x0132CCA0 were not traced, so the directory of the per-character files is not recorded. The xivl-decomp tracked config tool shows config.sys and a screenshots path under the Personal folder, and their relation to this root is unknown.
The origin of the character id that 0x004DCC41 passes to 0x004D9980 was not traced.
The object passed as the constructor's fourth argument is identified as SystemConfig by its group 9 key 12 record only.
The SystemConfig load path, including whether config.sys is its file, was not traced.
The constructor at 0x00860A70 registers a character record in a Config store with a version and appearancetype keys. It is not a user config store and its rows are not recorded here.
The caller set of the five group 3 volume keys reset by 0x004D6A50 and the consumers of every key name were not traced.
The range words are never enforced on the paths traced here. Whether a widget script clamps them was not traced.
